summary: CCC-built 1938 lookout in Polk County with a stone base and wooden cab; the cab was dismantled in a restoration halted by the 2000 ice storm, and NRHP listing was removed in 2005.

facts.design: Single-story stone base with a live-in wooden cab and catwalk; cab given as 12 by 12 ft in the register and about 14 by 14 ft in a 2007 update
facts.status_note: The wooden cab was dismantled; by 2007 only the catwalk had been rebuilt, and a 2019 visit found the top structure missing.

access.note: No closure is mentioned in any source read; the route is rough and unsigned

visit.trail_note: Rough, unsigned path; an experienced ATV driver can manage it, and hikers should expect overgrowth and insects (2019 visit report).

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Ouachita National Forest (Mena Ranger District)

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; the register, Central US Lookouts and the Encyclopedia caption all give 1938
Wooden cab dismantled during a restoration that the 2000 ice storm halted; the update gives no exact year, so 2000 is approximate
Delisted from the National Register of Historic Places, per a 2007 update on the register page
Visit report: top structure, both windows and first-floor door missing; no staff

evidence.supports: built by the CCC in 1938; nearly identical to Tall Peak
evidence.quote: Bee Mountain Lookout is nearly identical to Tall Peak (US No. 183) and was also built by the CCC in 1938.

evidence.supports: single-story stone base with a live-in wooden cab; style described as unique to the Southern Region
evidence.quote: The single-story stone base (with room) supports a live-in 12’ x 12’ wooden cab with catwalk of a style that was unique to the Southern Region of the U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: 2007 update gives the cab as about 14 by 14 feet
evidence.quote: The wooden cab was approximately 14 feet by 14 feet

evidence.supports: 2007 update calls the tower two-story, one of a pair
evidence.quote: it is one of a pair of unique wood and stone two-story fire towers

evidence.supports: 2007 update calls Tall Peak its twin
evidence.quote: The district plans to restore its twin, Tall Peak Lookout Tower, and place it in the rental program.

evidence.supports: 12 by 12 frame cabin on a rock foundation, built by CCC members in 1938
evidence.quote: 1938: A 12 x 12 frame lookout cabin was built atop a rock foundation by members of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: in Polk County, built 1938
evidence.quote: Bee Mountain Lookout in the Ouachita National Forest in Polk County, built in 1938.

evidence.supports: stone base and wooden cab in a style more often found in western states
evidence.quote: These two have short stone bases with wooden cabs built in a style more often found in western states.

evidence.supports: stabilization plan: replace cedar shingles, redo stairs and catwalk, with volunteers and Forest Service staff
evidence.quote: the district planned to stabilize the structure (e.g. replacing the cedar shingles and redoing the staircase and catwalk) with the assistance of both local volunteers and Forest Service employees.

evidence.supports: plan became full restoration; wooden cab dismantled
evidence.quote: Midway through the stabilization project, the decision was made to completely restore the tower and the wooden cab was dismantled.

evidence.supports: 2000 ice storm halted the work
evidence.quote: Shortly thereafter the district was hit by the 2000 Ice Storm and work was stopped.

evidence.supports: only the catwalk rebuilt as of 2007
evidence.quote: To date only the catwalk has been rebuilt.

evidence.supports: delisted from the NRHP in 2005
evidence.quote: was delisted from the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) in 2005.

evidence.supports: reason for delisting: lost essential physical features
evidence.quote: Since the fire tower no longer retains much of its essential physical features, the tower no longer meets the eligibility criteria

evidence.supports: register description still says the site is on the NRHP
evidence.quote: Extensively vandalized, the site is also on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.supports: lists three NRHP-listed towers in Arkansas; Bee Mountain is not one
evidence.quote: Arkansas also has three towers listed on the National Register of Historic Places: Crossroads Fire Tower (listed in 2006), Sugarloaf Fire Tower Historic District (listed in 1995) and Tall Peak Fire Tower (listed in 1993).

evidence.supports: 2019 visit: first-floor door, both windows and top structure missing
evidence.quote: First floor door missing, both windows missing, some debris inside on the floor, top structure missing

evidence.supports: catwalk planks look questionable (2019)
evidence.quote: the wooden planks that span the ceiling seem questionable

evidence.supports: no staff
evidence.quote: No staff; this explains the squalor of the structure.

evidence.supports: rough path; ATV can manage; hikers warned about overgrowth and insects
evidence.quote: Very rough path to the structure. An experienced ATV driver can make the trip up fine, but hikers should be wary of the overgrowth and insects.

evidence.supports: no signs guide the path to the structure
evidence.quote: there are NO signs that guide the path to the structure

evidence.supports: registered on the NHLR on July 16, 1996
tower lies on the Mena Ranger District; the Mena district is the one to check with before a visit
evidence.quote: a fire tower located on the Mena Ranger District of the Ouachita National Forest

evidence.supports: the visit report is dated July 7, 2019
evidence.quote: July 7, 2019

notes_for_editor: Read: the NHLR page (it includes the 2007 update and the 2019 visit report), Central US Lookouts, the Encyclopedia of Arkansas caption and forest-lookouts entry, and Preserve Arkansas. Open conflicts: cab 12 by 12 ft (register description, Central US Lookouts) vs about 14 by 14 ft (2007 update); single-story base (register description) vs two-story (2007 update). NRHP: the register description says still listed, but the 2007 update says delisted in 2005; the story follows the delisting. The 2000 dismantling date is approximate. No source found for fire-watch years or the last staffing. Access level public is inferred from the absence of any closure, not stated by a source. Current condition rests on the 2019 visit; no newer report found. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used.
